title: Foresee-to-Ground: From Predictive Temporal Perception to Evidence-Driven Reasoning for Video Temporal Grounding
claim: Prior methods emit timestamps directly from a token stream; ours first identifies event evidence, then measures boundaries on it.
layout: 3 panels: two small prior panels on top, large ours below; left-to-right flow
description: The figure has three panels. Panels (a) and (b) sit side by side at the top, separated by dashed lines. Each is a short left-to-right block diagram. Icons for video, query and time metadata feed colored encoder boxes. These produce a dashed stack of colored token bars that goes into a gray LLM block and then to an answer icon. Panel (b) adds a yellow temporal encoder and temporal decoder plus a blue detokenize block. Panel (c) fills the bottom and is much larger. It is labeled as ours. A lower gray box, Perception, shows an uncertainty curve with red spikes at event transitions and yellow candidate segments. These feed an upper gray box, Reasoning, with red dashed Identify and Measure stages. Orange, yellow and blue token groups carry the color coding. The eye goes first to the big panel (c).
caption: Paradigms for VTG with Video-LLMs. (a) Direct timestamp generation; (b) Direct timestamp generation with time-text interface; (c) F2G: a verifiable grounding pipeline.
abstract: Current Video-LLM approaches for Video Temporal Grounding (VTG) typically rely on direct timestamp generation from an unstructured visual-token stream, often leading to brittle numerics and inconsistent boundaries. To address this, we propose Foresee-to-Ground (F2G), a framework that reformulates VTG as a verifiable Identify-then-Measure problem. F2G integrates Predictive Temporal Perception with Evidence-Driven Reasoning: it learns boundary-sensitive temporal representations to build a video-wide evidence pool of candidate event segments, and exposes these segments to the LLM as citable evidence units that bind boundary prediction to explicit event hypotheses. By decoupling event identification from precise boundary measurement, F2G stabilizes grounding and makes predictions verifiable. Extensive experiments demonstrate that F2G consistently improves grounding accuracy across diverse benchmarks, transfers robustly across different Video-LLM backbones, and preserves general video understanding capabilities.
